title: Chat Completions vs Responses: choosing and migrating
summary: Choose the API from four dials: model family, state ownership, portability and retention. Migrating means changing message shapes, reading output Items and deciding where state lives.
useIf: You pick an API for a new build, plan a migration, or map an Assistants or Azure app to current APIs.
avoidIf: You treat Responses as a renamed Chat Completions. It changes state, tools, reasoning handling and several parameters.

explain.md: Four dials decide the choice. **Model family**: reasoning models with tools on GPT-5.4 and later need Responses. **State ownership**: your app resends history (Chat Completions), or the server holds it (Responses with `previous_response_id` or Conversations). **Portability**: Chat-style messages are the common format across vendors. **Retention**: server state conflicts with a no-retention policy unless you replay statelessly [[r6]] [[r7]] [[r10]].

explain.title: Migration steps from Chat Completions to Responses

steps.title: 1. Reshape input
steps.md: Move the `system` message to `instructions` and the rest to `input`.

steps.title: 2. Rename formats
steps.md: `response_format` becomes `text.format`. Read all `output` Items, not index 0.

steps.title: 3. Port the tool loop
steps.md: Handle `function_call` and `function_call_output` Items. Check strict behaviour.

steps.title: 4. Choose state
steps.md: Replay yourself, `previous_response_id`, or Conversations. Review retention.

steps.title: 5. Drop what is gone
steps.md: Responses has no `seed`, `stop`, `n`, penalties, `logit_bias` or `top_k`. Move to prompts, schemas and tests.

steps.title: 6. Re-evaluate
steps.md: Run your evals. Caching, reasoning context and tool behaviour can shift results.

explain.md: **Azure**: since August 2025 you can opt in to the v1 API. Use the `OpenAI()` client with a base URL ending `/openai/v1`, and `api-version` is no longer required. Azure recommends Responses for Azure OpenAI models and keeps responses 30 days with deletion by ID [[r14]] [[r34]]. **Anthropic**: Messages is stateless, `max_tokens` is required, content is typed blocks (`text`, `tool_use`, `tool_result`, `thinking`) and caching uses `cache_control` [[r19]].

explain.title: The Assistants API is gone on OpenAI
explain.md: Deprecation was announced on 2025-08-26 and the API was sunset on 2026-08-26. Threads map to Conversations and Runs to Responses. The migration guide maps Assistants to Prompts, but reusable prompts are themselves deprecated with shutdown on 2026-11-30, so hold instructions and tools in your code or config. Azure OpenAI Assistants are documented to retire on 2026-08-26 with migration to Foundry Agent Service. Azure status after that date is unverified [[r51]] [[r11]] [[r49]].

Interviews: justify an API choice from dials, not preference

use: Responses for new builds, reasoning plus tools, built-in tools, background jobs and server state
Chat Completions for portability, simple stateless chat and `seed` or penalties
Anthropic Messages for Claude features, behind an adapter if you are multi-vendor
avoid: Migrating everything at once without evals
Standardising on Responses when most traffic goes to vendors that lack it
Depending on Assistants or reusable prompts
flips: A model upgrade breaks tools with reasoning on Chat: move that route to Responses
A no-retention policy appears: switch to stateless replay with encrypted reasoning
You drop all non-OpenAI vendors: simplify to Responses

pitfalls.cause: It reads `output[0]`, which may be a reasoning or tool Item
pitfalls.fix: Iterate Items or use the SDK helper for output text

pitfalls.cause: `seed`, `stop`, penalties and `logit_bias` do not exist in Responses
pitfalls.fix: Replace them with prompts, schemas and repeated-run tests

pitfalls.cause: All earlier input tokens are billed again
pitfalls.fix: Trim, compact or cache a stable prefix, and measure per conversation

pitfalls.symptom: Old Azure samples fail or look wrong
pitfalls.fix: Use the v1 API with `OpenAI()` and a `/openai/v1` base URL

scenarios.title: An Assistants app after the sunset
scenarios.situation: A support product built on the OpenAI Assistants API (threads, runs, a stored assistant with tools) starts failing after 2026-08-26.
unknowns: How many threads need to be carried over?
scenarios.question: What is the migration path?

options.name: Move to Responses, map threads to Conversations and runs to Responses, and keep instructions and tool definitions in code or config
options.why: It follows the documented mapping and avoids Prompts, which are deprecated with a 2026-11-30 shutdown.
options.tradeoff: You rebuild the run loop and test tool behaviour.

options.name: Map each assistant to a reusable Prompt
options.why: It is the documented mapping in the migration guide.
options.tradeoff: Reusable prompts shut down on 2026-11-30, so you migrate twice.

options.name: Keep calling the Assistants API and wait for a notice
options.why: OpenAI sunset it on 2026-08-26 and says it is no longer available.
options.tradeoff: Waiting is only reasonable on a platform with a later published date.

flips.then: Check Azure's current notice and consider Foundry Agent Service, since post-date status is unverified.
Replay statelessly instead of using Conversations.

scenarios.takeaway: Move state to Conversations and keep definitions in your own code.

scenarios.title: One feature needs GPT-6 tools, the rest is portable
scenarios.situation: A product calls several vendors through Chat Completions. One new feature needs web search and tools with a GPT-6 reasoning model.
constraints: One feature needs built-in web search and reasoning with tools
unknowns: How much traffic does the new feature carry?
Will other vendors gain similar tools?
scenarios.question: How do you proceed?

options.name: Rewrite the whole product on Responses at once
options.why: It puts portable traffic at risk without evals and does not help vendors that lack Responses.
options.tradeoff: A full move is right when OpenAI is the only vendor.

options.name: Add a Responses path for the new feature behind an adapter and keep Chat elsewhere
options.why: It isolates platform features, limits risk and keeps portability for the rest.
options.tradeoff: Two code paths to maintain and test.

options.name: Stay on Chat Completions with effort `none` and write your own search tool
options.tradeoff: You give up reasoning and built-in tools, and you own the search tool.

flips.if: The new feature becomes most of the traffic
flips.then: Move the main path to Responses.

flips.if: Quality tests show reasoning adds nothing
flips.then: The Chat plus own tool path is cheaper to run.

scenarios.takeaway: Isolate platform-specific features behind an adapter.

quiz.q: Match each Assistants concept to its replacement.
quiz.explain: OpenAI's migration guide maps threads to Conversations, runs to Responses and assistants to Prompts, which are also deprecated. Azure documents migration to Foundry Agent Service.

quiz.q: Which Chat Completions parameters have no equivalent in the Responses body?
quiz.explain: Responses has `temperature` but no `seed`, `stop`, `n`, penalties, `logit_bias` or `top_k`.

quiz.q: Which change most strongly pushes a Chat Completions agent to Responses?
options: Adopting GPT-5.4 or later with reasoning effort above `none` and tools
quiz.explain: From GPT-5.4, Chat Completions does not support tools with reasoning effort other than `none`. `seed` exists only on Chat.
